w08.003: Where Appendix III divided the master universe by space, Appendix IV divides the same master universe by time. The Urantia Book speaks of a Havona age, a superuniverse age, and outer universe ages; Sadler pairs these with the six space levels and arrives at six universe ages. He then follows experiential Deity, God the Sevenfold, Havona, the superuniverses, the local universes, the Trinity-related sons, and the finaliters through these ages, setting the text's own statements beside his inferences.
w08.004: 1. Six Universe Ages and Six Space Levels (orig. pp. 190–192)
w08.006: The Urantia Book calls time and space a “conjoined mechanism” of the master universe [118:9.1]. If the six space levels are the great divisions of space, the universe ages are the great divisions of time. The text names them in this order:
w08.008: Sadler assigns one outer universe age to each of the four outer space levels and so counts six ages in all. The first age belongs to the Havona space level, the second to the superuniverse space level, and the third through the sixth to the Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, and Quartan Space Levels. We live now in the second age, the superuniverse age. In Sadler's pairing of time and space, the dawning of each new age means the opening and development of a new space level. Something will doubtless follow the sixth age, but since it lies beyond the completion of the master universe, he gives it a name of its own: the post-ultimate age.
w08.009: The six universe ages, the six space levels, and the experiential Deity that grows in each age (Sadler's arrangement)
w08.010: The first age: no beginning, yet an end
w08.011: Sadler recalls that the Zero Age of Appendix I was never a real age, only a starting point for thought, and he reads the text's phrase “⟦Q 31:9.3⟧the dawn of eternity⟦/Q⟧” [31:9.3] as the “hypothetical beginning” of a Havona age that in fact had none.
w08.012: The first age is unique in several respects. Like the central universe itself, it belongs to past eternity and has no beginning in time. It is pre-supreme and pre-ultimate, hence pre-experiential, and therefore wholly existential. Sadler regards it as pre-creational and pre-evolutionary as well, on the ground that the Havona natives, though offspring of the Trinity, are described as beings “⟦Q 14:4.10⟧who never were created⟦/Q⟧” [14:4.10].
w08.013: Yet the first age does have an end. Sadler surmises that its boundary fell near the trinitization of the Ancients of Days, or perhaps at the moment when the Trinity commissioned the organization of the seven superuniverses.
w08.015: The five ages that follow the first Sadler gathers under one name, the post-Havona ages. Each has a beginning and an end in time, and all are experiential. The Urantia Book places the actualization of experiential Deity in exactly this period:
w08.017: Sadler notes a further mark of these ages: a procession moving in two directions at once. In the present age the Supreme Creators come down while evolutionary creatures climb upward. In the next age the finaliters will go out into outer space, and beings native to outer space will ascend inward by way of the perfected superuniverses.
w08.018: The uniqueness of the second age and the enlargement of destiny
w08.019: The present age is unique too, for it is the age in which the Supreme Being evolves and grows. When that growth is complete the age will close, and the chance to share in it will not come again.
w08.021: Sadler also observes that successive ages enlarge destiny: each age lets its successor pass beyond the growth limits of the one before. The text offers Havona as the pattern.
w08.023: 2. Experiential Deity Age by Age (orig. pp. 192–196)
w08.024: In the first age there is no experiential Deity; every later age is marked by its growth. Sadler collects the textual clues under four periods, and the table below condenses them.
w08.025: Experiential Deity across the ages (the gist of the textual clues Sadler assembles)
w08.027: Present in Havona as a spirit personality; acts as a sovereign power-personality in the grand universe; not yet findable
First and second both limited realities
Present in Havona in a subabsolute, superpersonal sense
w08.028: Emerges and becomes contactable; replaces the Ancients of Days as superuniverse sovereign
The first experiential Trinity forms as a fact
Approaches as the challenge of the next age
w08.029: Third function on the master universe scale; superalmighty of the outer universes
The first experiential Trinity co-ordinates the master universe
Power-personalized as sovereign of the master universe
w08.030: The Trinity Absolute forms as a fact
Leading on to the revelation of God the Absolute?
w08.031: With each age the object of the great challenge changes. For us the challenge now is to find God the Supreme, but for the finaliters God the Ultimate already looms as the next one. The text says that God the Ultimate foreshadows his transcendental overcontrol during the later stages of a local universe settled in light and life [56:7.5]. As for the third function of the Supreme Being, the revelators themselves concede, “⟦Q 116:0.5⟧But none of us really know⟦/Q⟧” [116:0.5]. Sadler, for his part, lists three conjectures and declines to choose among them.
w08.032: 3. God the Sevenfold and the Future of the Supreme Creators (orig. pp. 196–199)
w08.034: The universe relationships of the Paradise Deities are not altered by the experiential development of the universes. Sadler therefore turns to the Supreme Creators within God the Sevenfold—the Master Spirits, the Creator Sons, and the Ancients of Days—and asks what lies ahead for them. His starting point is this passage:
w08.036: The text says that as the creations of time settle, God the Supreme functions more fully while the activity of the Supreme Creators recedes in proportion. Will they then go out into outer space? The text leaves the question open: “⟦Q 56:7.6⟧We do not know⟦/Q⟧” [56:7.6].
w08.038: **The Seven Master Spirits.** Taken together, the Master Spirits bear the attributes of Supreme, Ultimate, and Supreme-Ultimate, and from this Sadler infers that they have the capacity to function as far as the post-ultimate age. The text says that the Ancients of Days and the Master Spirits are “⟦Q 0:8.11⟧probably eternally fixed as permanent administrators in the grand universe⟦/Q⟧” [0:8.11], but Sadler reads this as a fixing of residence rather than of the range of activity. His warrant is the statement that the executive abodes of the Master Spirits are the Paradise headquarters of the seven superuniverses “⟦Q 13:4.6⟧and their correlated segments in outer space⟦/Q⟧” [13:4.6].
w08.039: **The Ancients of Days.** Because the evolution of the Supreme is still incomplete, they now provide full administrative overcontrol [18:3.9]. When this age ends, the Supreme Being, the experiential sovereign, will take their place, and they will become his vicegerents.
w08.041: **The Universe Sons and Universe Spirits.** The text describes the relation of the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit this way:
w08.043: Sadler holds that this relation is being worked out in practice less by the Son and Spirit of Paradise than by the Creator Son and Creative Spirit of each local universe. The text reports the view that future ages may bring a closer union between the two, from which a new associate creator of ultimate nature might eventuate [56:7.7], and it conjectures that the Creator Sons are destined to function in the outer universes. The thought that the Master Michaels may one day move their status sphere from Sonarington to Vicegerington is Sadler's own guess and has no basis in the text.
w08.045: Sadler views the central universe from four vantage points: yesterday, today, tomorrow, and the far future.
w08.046: The four faces of Havona, from the first age to the post-ultimate age (dashed outlines mark Sadler's inferences)
w08.047: **Yesterday.** In the first age Havona underwent no evolutionary change [106:0.18], and it needed no power centers. It was a perfect creation, though one bounded by its own perfection.
w08.048: **Today.** Present-day Havona is no longer the Havona of yesterday. The spirit personality of the Supreme has appeared; the organization of the superuniverses has brought changes, and the arrival of the Grandfanda has brought more. The Circuit Spirits have come into view at their work, the graduate guides and the secondary supernaphim have appeared, and citizens of Paradise have begun their outward pilgrimage through Havona. The text itself acknowledges the difference:
w08.050: **Tomorrow.** The needs of tomorrow already show in the Havona of today. The Universal Censors stationed on each of the billion worlds are thought to be placed with an eye to future ages, when the population of Havona will change [19:4.2]. The Havona natives may someday cease to enter the Corps of the Finality, and the residents of Havona may become mixed [19:6.4]. From this Sadler infers that in the post-supreme ages Havona will become a training universe for absonite beings.
w08.052: **The far future.** Sadler concludes that even in the post-ultimate age, after the master universe is complete, Havona will remain the pattern of divine perfection. The text likewise voices the opinion that “⟦Q 14:6.41⟧the potentials of eternal Havona are really unlimited⟦/Q⟧” [14:6.41].
w08.053: 5. The Ages of the Superuniverses and Local Universes (orig. pp. 202–208)
w08.054: From the first age into the second
w08.055: Sadler reconstructs the passage from the first age to the second in four stages. The text gives no chronology; he weaves scattered clues into a plausible order.
w08.056: **The unqualified first age.** The Third Source and Center becomes eternal together with Havona, and the Havona natives have no origin.
w08.057: **The end of the first age.** The personalization of the Infinite Spirit closes the existential cycle of Deity personalization; the next personalization, the Seven Master Spirits, was subabsolute. Sadler takes the appearance of experiential beings as a sign that the first age is drawing to its close.
w08.058: **The era near eternity, the “dawn of time.”** The Solitary Messengers, the power directors and power centers, and the Reflective Spirits appear at about this time. Sadler reads the two expressions as naming one and the same period.
w08.059: **The beginning of superuniverse history.** The first entry in the Paradise records is the trinitization of the Ancients of Days; everything earlier belongs to prehistory.
w08.061: When the superuniverses settle in light and life, the Supreme Being becomes the experiential sovereign of the seven superuniverses. The text expresses the belief that the lines between the seven superuniverses will fade and that the grand universe will come to function as a perfected whole [117:7.15]. Sadler sees here a cosmic version of what happens on a single planet, where the evolutionary races develop separate cultures and then blend in the Adamic age. The Unqualified Supervisors of the Supreme become the high administrative body at superuniverse headquarters [55:12.3], and the work of the Supreme Creators lessens.
w08.062: Light and life is still not the end. The text calls the settled state only the growth limit “for the present universe age” and says that the next age will release the superuniverses from that limitation [106:0.18]. In the local universes, too, new relationships are developing among the Creator Sons, the Creative Spirits, the Teacher Sons, the Evening Stars, and the finaliters [55:10.9]. Sadler infers that all of them will one day serve together in outer space.
w08.063: Sadler raises one simple but pointed question as well. Ascenders from worlds that have passed the third stage of light and life receive a transient assignment on a planet still in the early stages of evolution [55:3.11]. What happens, then, when no such planets remain? The text gives no answer, but the question is a reminder that the local universes, too, must enter a new phase in the next age.
w08.064: 6. The Trinitized Sons and the Finaliters (orig. pp. 208–212)
w08.065: Beings who belong to other ages
w08.066: Some of the Trinity-related sons live in the present age yet hold the status of another.
w08.067: **Trinity-embraced sons.** The Mighty Messengers are “in status as of the preceding universe age” and do not share in the growth of the present one [117:2.4].
w08.068: **Creature-trinitized sons.** They are born and live now, yet are held in reserve for the age to come.
w08.070: **Trinitized sons of destiny.** They embody concepts that transcend the creative limits of the present universe age, and all are held in reserve on Vicegerington [22:7.14].
w08.071: Within a single age, in other words, beings of several ages live side by side.
w08.072: The three ages of the finaliter
w08.073: **The second age.** On entering the Corps of the Finality, the ascender passes through the experience called finaliter transcendation, becomes allied in a new way with the spirit-gravity circuit of the Eternal Son, and becomes a candidate for recognition as a personality of God the Supreme [117:5.3]. Sadler suspects a link between this event and the statement that, at the sixth stage of spirit existence, a certain liaison factor of the mind passes into the experiential endowment of the Supreme [107:5.6].
w08.074: **The post-supreme ages.** The destiny of the finaliters lies in outer space. The text expresses the belief that Adjuster-fused mortals, together with their finaliter associates, are destined to take part in administering the first outer space level [112:7.17]. The native beings of the outer universes will not share in the growth of the Supreme, and the finaliters will make good that lack. On attaining the seventh stage of spirit existence, their dual minds will be joined to the mind of the Supreme and so become triune.
w08.075: **The post-ultimate age.** Here Sadler turns to the seventh dimension of mortal personality.
w08.077: Add to this the “phase of qualified potential absoluteness” conferred by fusion with the Adjuster [112:7.1], and Sadler's conclusion is plain: nothing will halt the growth of the finaliters, even after the master universe is complete.
w08.078: Sadler and the Text: Corrected References
w08.079: Appendix IV contains several misprinted references. The passage stating that the function of God the Sevenfold dates from the organization of the seven superuniverses is 0:8.12 (printed in the original as 0:10.12 and 0:13.12). The status of the Mighty Messengers is given at 117:2.4 and that of the creature-trinitized sons at 117:2.3 (printed as 17:2.4 and 172:3.14). The passage on the sequence of ages is 115:3.18 (printed as 15:3.18), and the Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy appear at 18:1.1 (printed as 8:1.1). For the trinitized sons of destiny this book cites 22:7.14, where their relation to the Architects of the Master Universe is described.
w08.080: Sadler divides the time of the master universe into six universe ages and pairs each with one of the six space levels. We live in the second, the superuniverse age.
w08.081: The first age, the Havona age, has no beginning but has an end, and it is wholly existential. The other five, the post-Havona ages, are all experiential.
w08.082: The second age is the one age in which the Supreme Being evolves; once it ends, the opportunity to share in that growth will not return.
w08.083: Successive ages enlarge destiny. Havona moves from static perfection to a changing universe and then toward a training universe for absonite beings, while light and life is only the growth limit of the present age.
w08.084: Trinity-embraced sons, creature-trinitized sons, and trinitized sons of destiny all live now, yet each holds the status of a different age.
w08.085: The finaliters are destined to reveal the Supreme in outer space, and Sadler infers that their growth continues into the post-ultimate age.
w08.087: Appendix V, Dual-Deity in the Universe Ages (pp. 213–220)
w08.088: Sadler uses the term Dual-Deity for Deity working in pairs, as distinct from the Trinity, in which three are bound into one. His formula is brief: Dual-Deity pioneers, and the Trinity consolidates. He reads the six partnerships named in 106:8.12—the chain that runs from Father-Son to Absolute and Father-Infinite—against the sequence of the universe ages.
w08.089: 1. Dual-Deity Pioneers, the Trinity Consolidates (orig. pp. 213–214)
w08.090: Both the Father-Son partnership and the Paradise Trinity have existed from past eternity.
w08.092: As Sadler reads the order of events, the Father-Son first trinitize the Infinite Spirit and eternalize Havona, but it is the Paradise Trinity that brings the work to completion. The central creation is therefore of Trinity origin and is governed by beings of Trinity origin.
w08.093: The same pattern recurs in the local universe, the work of a Creator Son and a Creative Spirit—an achievement of Dual-Deity. Will the Trinity complete the work here as well? Sadler thinks so, and he finds a hint in the discussion of the Solitary Messengers in Paper 23.
w08.095: When the outer universe of the frontier is finished and becomes an inner universe, the single- and dual-origin pioneers move on to a new frontier and Trinity-origin administrators take their place. A small example is the growing role of the Union of Days in a local universe once it reaches light and life [55:10.1]. Pioneering and settling: such is the division of labor between Dual-Deity and the Trinity.
w08.096: 2. The Chain of Six Partnerships (orig. pp. 214–215)
w08.098: The idea that Dual-Deity partnerships follow one another in sequence is not Sadler's invention; the text states it outright.
w08.100: Sadler maps the six onto ages and universes. Father-Son belongs to the first age and Havona; Son-Spirit to the second age and the seven hundred thousand local universes; Spirit-Supreme to the four outer space levels. Supreme-Ultimate can function only after the Ultimate has emerged, that is, once the master universe is complete, and the last two lie further still in the future. The text gives only the sequence, not its correlation with the ages, so the correlation is Sadler's interpretation.
w08.101: The six Dual-Deity partnerships: from existential to experiential and back toward the existential (the correlation with the ages is Sadler's interpretation)
w08.102: From existential to experiential, and back again
w08.103: Sadler traces a curve along this chain. Father-Son is the only wholly existential partnership. Son-Spirit may be existential on Paradise, but the pairing of Universe Son and Universe Spirit in a local universe is experiential and evolutionary. Spirit-Supreme is at least half experiential, and Sadler expects that in practice it will be a collaboration of the Supreme Being with the Master Spirits; in that case the pair would be wholly experiential.
w08.104: Supreme-Ultimate stands as the one partnership that is wholly experiential, the counterpart of the wholly existential Father-Son. After it the chain turns back toward the existential. The final pair, Absolute and Father-Infinite, is eternal like the first and seems to have neither origin nor completion. In this circling shape Sadler finds the reason the text calls the chain “the completion of the cycle of reality.”
w08.106: Sadler also reads in this chain God's desire to share creative initiative with His co-ordinates and associates. In Havona the Father takes the lead; in the local universes the Sons lead with the Spirits as partners; in outer space the Spirits will lead with the Supreme Being in support. Sadler names this sequence the Processional of Initiative.
w08.109: The eternal Father-Son partnership is the archetype of every Dual-Deity relationship. It trinitizes the Infinite Spirit, is united with the Spirit as the Paradise Trinity, and at the same time brings forth the perfect central universe. Because Havona is an “eternity event,” there never was a time when dual-origin administrators governed it. The worlds of the Father are ruled by the Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy and the billion worlds of Havona by the Eternals of Days—all of Trinity origin.
w08.111: The Son-Spirit partnership concerns the evolutionary growth of local universes that were incomplete from the start. The first partnership was completed in eternity, on Paradise; the second moves toward completion in time, through evolution. Sadler infers that at the end of the second age this completion will take the following form:
w08.112: The seven hundred thousand local universes attain finite perfection and are settled in light and life.
w08.113: The seven hundred thousand pairs of Universe Sons and Universe Spirits achieve a trinitizing union.
w08.114: Each union yields an associate creator, co-ordinate with the Son and the Spirit—seven hundred thousand in all.
w08.115: A new creative association thus arises for service in outer space: seven hundred thousand Son-Spirit Creative Trios.
w08.116: Just as Father-Son trinitized an equal Deity, the Infinite Spirit, and found completion in the Paradise Trinity, so Son-Spirit is to be completed by a like act; such is the symmetry Sadler sees. All four points are his inferences rather than statements of the text, whose only support is the cautious view, noted earlier from 56:7.7, of a new “associate-creator identity.”
w08.117: Once formed, a Dual-Deity partnership does not come to an end. Father-Son goes on working as the source of the Creator Sons after the first age has closed, and Son-Spirit continues in new pairings in the outer universes. Partnerships are not replaced; they accumulate.
w08.119: Sadler detects one more dual relationship in the second age. On one side stands triune Paradise Deity, eternally one in the Paradise Trinity; on the other, the whole company of Supreme Creators. The text calls the Supreme Being the synthesizer of “⟦Q 0:7.9⟧triune Paradise Deity in experiential association with the Supreme Creators of time and space⟦/Q⟧” [0:7.9]. Sadler expects the Supreme Creators, taken collectively, to evolve a single Deity reality destined to take its place within the first experiential Trinity, and he reads the relation between that collective and the Paradise Trinity as one form of Dual-Deity.
w08.122: The Spirit-Supreme partnership can hardly function in the present age, since the Supreme Being has not yet been actualized as Deity. Sadler calls it the first wholly future partnership in the chain. The text says almost nothing about this pairing, but it speaks more than once of the close relation between the Infinite Spirit and the Supreme.
w08.124: The Seven Master Spirits have a share in this closeness, above all the seventh, who speaks for the Supreme. Sadler infers that the Supreme Being will collaborate with the Master Spirits throughout the transcendental unfolding of all four outer space levels, and he anticipates that this collaboration will multiply creative diversity by seven at every step.
w08.125: Sadler's projected expansion of creative diversity (interaction of the seven natures of the Master Spirits)
w08.132: The original prints the figure for the Tertiary Space Level as 2,041; since seven to the fourth power is 2,401, the number is corrected here. The sevenfold diversity of the superuniverses rests on the text's statement that the Master Spirits express “⟦Q 16:3.1⟧the seven possible associations of triune Deity⟦/Q⟧” [16:3.1]; the multiplication beyond that point is Sadler's own design.
w08.133: The two earlier partnerships were completed by trinitization. Will Spirit-Supreme be completed in the same way? Sadler thinks not. The emergence of God the Ultimate follows from the first experiential Trinity's becoming unified [106:4.2], not from a union of Spirit and Supreme. The fruit of this collaboration is rather the continued growth of the Supreme on transcendental levels, in preparation for membership in the second experiential Trinity.
w08.134: Three partnerships beyond the master universe
w08.135: The remaining three belong to the time after the master universe is complete. Supreme-Ultimate resembles Father-Son: each is completed by a trinitization of Deity and gives rise to a new Trinity. From Father-Son came God the Spirit and the Paradise Trinity; from Supreme-Ultimate, in Sadler's scheme, will come God the Absolute and the third experiential Trinity. Ultimate-Absolute tends the continuing growth of the Cosmos Infinite, and Absolute and Father-Infinite is a relation of the eternal future that may or may not come to pass.
w08.136: A Note: Dual-Deity within the Triunities
w08.137: In a footnote Sadler points out that three of the seven triunities contain a Dual-Deity. The second, the power-pattern triunity, has Father-Son as its first member, and the third, the spirit-evolutional triunity, has Son-Spirit. Of the third triunity the text says that “⟦Q 104:4.21⟧the Son-Spirit functions as active creative spirit⟦/Q⟧” [104:4.21]. The fourth, the triunity of energy infinity, introduces a pairing not met before: Father-Spirit. Sadler connects this pair with Solitarington, the status sphere of beings of Father-Spirit origin; though the Father may have had no part in their creation, “⟦Q 13:1.16⟧in this universe age he does have to do with their function⟦/Q⟧” [13:1.16].
w08.138: Dual-Deity is Sadler's term for Deity working in pairs. He reads the ages through the principle that Dual-Deity pioneers and the Trinity consolidates.
w08.139: The chain of six partnerships comes from 106:8.12; Sadler correlates its links in turn with Havona, the grand universe, the outer universes, and the time beyond the master universe.
w08.140: The chain traces a circle: from existential Father-Son, through wholly experiential Supreme-Ultimate, back toward the existential.
w08.141: Sadler infers that the Son-Spirit partnership will be completed at the end of the second age in seven hundred thousand Son-Spirit Creative Trios.
w08.142: Spirit-Supreme is the first wholly future partnership; Sadler expects the joint work of the Master Spirits with the Supreme Being to multiply creative diversity by seven at each level.
w08.143: Once formed, partnerships do not end but accumulate, and creative initiative is shared ever more widely.
w08.144: Total Deity Through the Universe Ages
w08.145: Appendix VI, Total Deity in the Universe Ages (pp. 221–233)
w08.146: Appendix V dealt with the pioneering of Dual-Deity; Appendix VI follows the consolidating function of Total Deity through the ages. Sadler gathers the seven levels of 0:1.3–1.10 into three groups—pre-creative, outgoing, and incoming levels—and finds that the scheme fits past eternity and the present age well but falters before Havona. As a remedy he tentatively proposes a different set of seven levels suited to the Havona age, which he calls the Existential Mechanism.
w08.147: 1. Gathering Seven Levels into Three (orig. pp. 221–224)
w08.149: The Foreword of The Urantia Book says that Total Deity functions on seven levels.
w08.151: The levels are named static, potential, associative, creative, evolutional, supreme, and finally ultimate. Sadler takes the order as meaningful and divides it into three groups.
w08.152: **Pre-creative levels**: static, potential, associative. On these levels Deity functioned before the master universe existed.
w08.153: **Outgoing levels**: creative and evolutional. Here Deity gives of itself and expands outward.
w08.154: **Incoming levels**: supreme and ultimate. These gather up, on finite and absonite levels, all that the outgoing levels have unfolded and draw it into unity. On the supreme level finite reality is power-personalized in the Supreme Being, while on the ultimate level absonite reality is power-personalized in God the Ultimate.
w08.155: The image of breathing may help. If the pre-creative levels are the pause before a breath, the outgoing levels are the exhalation and the incoming levels the inhalation. God the Ultimate works “⟦Q 0:2.17⟧on final creative levels of Deity reality⟦/Q⟧” [0:2.17], so whatever lies beyond would be a supercreative level—precisely the word the text applies to God the Absolute [0:2.18].
w08.157: Sadler retraces the path of Appendix I within this framework. The stage Before Pre-Zero, a hypothetical static instant without even potential, corresponds to the static level. In the Pre-Zero stage the Deity Absolute and the Unqualified Absolute separate and the potential level appears, while the activity of the Universal Absolute, which holds the two together, is the first form of the associative level. In the Zero Age this level becomes personal through the association of Father and Son, and in the first age it is completed when the Infinite Spirit appears and the Paradise Trinity is formed. Up to this point all goes smoothly. The difficulty is Havona.
w08.158: 2. The Paradox of Havona and the Existential Mechanism (orig. pp. 224–228)
w08.160: Havona seems to be a perfect universe created by the Trinity, yet the text says that its natives never were created. The text itself offers Havona as the best illustration of paradox.
w08.162: Sadler proposes to regard the creation of Havona as an act in eternity, in effect a pre-creative event. Two perspectives on Havona then emerge: the pre-creative Havona of the first age, when nothing lay outside it, and the post-creative Havona of the second age, which has entered into relations with the superuniverses and has received the Supreme and the Ultimate together with newer orders such as the Circuit Spirits and the secondary supernaphim. In its functioning, present-day Havona behaves exactly like a created pattern universe.
w08.163: A deeper problem remains. In the first age nothing was created and Havona did not evolve, so the creative and evolutional levels lay dormant. Yet the text says that the original Havona already held maximum finites, transcendental beings, and ultimate meanings [106:0.4–6], and life in Havona spans the range from the material to the absolute [14:4.2–8]. The Paradise Trinity of the first age, then, was already functioning on subabsolute levels—levels that are not the same as what we now call the supreme and ultimate levels. At this point the scheme of seven levels breaks down.
w08.165: Sadler's solution is to change the question. We may be applying an experiential yardstick to an existential situation. The seven levels may not be a framework valid for every age but merely the framework of the present one. The text itself gives such a warning:
w08.167: God, having free will, can modify the manifestations of His absoluteness [4:4.2], and the Paradise Trinity relates to the finite as the Trinity of Supremacy and to the absonite as the Trinity of Ultimacy [10:5.4–5]. Nothing, then, prevents the Trinity from having placed subabsolute reality within eternal Havona from the beginning. On this footing Sadler tentatively sets out seven levels of an Existential Mechanism suited to the first age.
w08.168: The Existential Mechanism proposed by Sadler for the first age, compared with the seven levels of The Urantia Book (the Experiential Mechanism)
w08.169: The first three levels are the same; the difference begins with the fourth. Sadler's Existential Mechanism continues with the transcendental, finite, ultimate, and absolute levels, and he gives reasons for this order. According to the text, the transcendental appears, “from the eternity viewpoint,” to have eventuated “⟦Q 105:7.1⟧in anticipation of the finite⟦/Q⟧” [105:7.1], so it precedes the finite. In the text's series of ultimate, coabsolute, and absolute, the ultimate comes before the absolute. The coabsolute, being a projection of experientials [106:0.7], drops out of a first age that knew no experience. The finite level then falls into the remaining fifth place.
w08.171: Sadler stresses that the finite level of the Existential Mechanism differs from the finite of the present age. The text distinguishes the perfect from the perfected.
w08.173: The inhabitants of Havona are primary maximums, arising from the fifth level of the Existential Mechanism; the perfected superuniverse ascenders are secondary maximums, arising from the fifth level of the Experiential Mechanism, the evolutional level. Both are finite, but the one is perfect from the start and the other becomes perfect through growth. Turning to the tertiary maximums that result from trinitizing relationships between the two [105:5.10], Sadler adds that there may be yet another way of viewing the levels.
w08.174: 3. The Experiential Mechanism and the Ages to Come (orig. pp. 228–233)
w08.176: In the post-Havona ages experiential Deity works alongside existential Deity. The text never says that experiential Deity functions on the static level, but it appears to function on the other six. That Deity should function on the evolutional level is hard to picture; Sadler points to the Thought Adjuster. “⟦Q 107:2.7⟧While retaining all of the character of the existential divine nature⟦/Q⟧” [107:2.7], the Adjuster indwells a human being, takes part in events on the evolutional level, and itself gains experience.
w08.177: Creation in the second age moves by two impulses. The first comes from Paradise-Havona, which sent forth the Ancients of Days and the Universe Sons and Spirits; the second comes from the efforts of these creators in time and space. The evolutional level is most fully displayed in the local universes, where even the Creators evolve [116:4.8], and the arrival of the Grandfanda carried evolutionary process into the perfect central creation itself.
w08.178: A quiet time between the ages
w08.179: The text speaks of a “space zone of comparative quiet” between neighboring space levels [12:1.14]. Sadler conjectures that there may likewise be a quiet time between the ages, and Paper 117 hints at the possibility:
w08.181: Sadler expects that in this quiet time the fully emerged Supreme Being will function completely on the supreme level of Total Deity and will enter into personal relations with the three Paradise Deities. Whatever unpredictability then remains will signal that the Ultimate and the Absolutes are present.
w08.182: The post-supreme ages: stretching the meaning of words
w08.183: In the four ages of outer space it becomes hard to fit the creative and evolutional levels to transcendental activity. The text says that the Transcendentalers neither create nor were created; they “⟦Q 31:8.3⟧simply eventuate⟦/Q⟧” [31:8.3].
w08.185: Sadler therefore proposes to widen the meaning of the creative level to include eventuation, and to widen the evolutional level to include growth that is superevolutionary yet not without experience—growth in transcended time. In his picture these enlarged outgoing levels reach into outer space, where the first experiential Trinity, the expanded God the Sevenfold, the third function of the Supreme, the emerging Ultimate, and the Trinity of Ultimacy all work together. When the master universe is complete and another quiet time arrives, the Trinity Ultimate reaches its final unification, God the Ultimate fully emerges, and the seventh level, the ultimate level, is complete.
w08.187: Beyond the ultimate level, thought moves outside the master universe. Since the Ultimate works on “final creative levels,” every transforming act beyond it is supercreative. If experience is projected beyond the master universe, that is the level the text calls coabsolute. Sadler foresees three new Deity realities in this domain—the second experiential Trinity, God the Absolute in trinitized expression, and the Trinity of Trinities—and expects them to operate by an entirely different Existential-Experiential Mechanism. The Existential Mechanism of the first age, the Experiential Mechanism of the present and near future, and the Existential-Experiential Mechanism beyond the ultimate: in these three mechanisms Sadler sums up his history of Total Deity.
w08.188: Sadler and the Text: The Honesty of Testing a Framework
w08.189: The merit of this appendix is that Sadler does not hide where his framework fails; instead, relying on the text's own reminder about “the standpoint of other universe ages,” he rebuilds the framework itself. The seven levels of the Existential Mechanism, however, are Sadler's proposal and do not appear in The Urantia Book, and he himself presents them only tentatively. Of the references in the original, 30:1.99 is correct as printed, while 0:3.18 should read 0:2.18.
w08.190: Sadler groups the seven levels of Total Deity into three: pre-creative (static, potential, associative), outgoing (creative, evolutional), and incoming (supreme, ultimate).
w08.191: The scheme serves well for tracing past eternity, but it falters before Havona, which held finite, transcendental, and ultimate realities from the beginning.
w08.192: Sadler suggests that the seven levels may be the Experiential Mechanism of the present age, and for the first age he tentatively proposes an Existential Mechanism of static, potential, associative, transcendental, finite, ultimate, and absolute levels.
w08.193: The inhabitants of Havona are primary maximums, perfect from the start; the superuniverse ascenders are secondary maximums, perfected through growth.
w08.194: In the post-supreme ages the meanings of words must be widened so that the creative level includes eventuation and the evolutional level includes transcendental growth.
w08.195: Beyond the ultimate, Sadler expects the second experiential Trinity, God the Absolute, and the Trinity of Trinities to function by a new Existential-Experiential Mechanism.
w09.002: Appendix VII, Mechanisms of Experiential Growth (pp. 234–248)
w09.003: Existential reality does not grow of itself; experiential reality does. In this appendix Sadler asks where growth comes from and by what route it finally reaches us. Everything new rises out of the Potential and is captured by the gravity circuits of the Actual, and between the two the Ultimate and the Supreme step absolute potentiality down to a magnitude that finite beings can use. Growth in the present age cannot be separated from the growth of the Supreme Being, and Sadler expects that once the Supreme has been completed, an altogether different kind of growth will begin in the outer space levels.
w09.005: The eternal Deities of Paradise have nothing left to grow into, for they already are all that they are. What grows is experiential reality, and experiential growth always involves two partners: it takes place when creator and creature work together. It is also contagious in a sense, for it can spread outward and call forth growth even within existential reality, which by itself never grows.
w09.006: With this in view, Sadler divides the history of the master universe into periods according to the manner in which growth occurs.
w09.007: The mechanisms of growth as Sadler distinguishes them
w09.009: No growth. Havona appeared in eternity without any work by the force organizers
w09.010: Finite evolutionary growth while the power-personalization of the Supreme is still incomplete
w09.011: Growth after the emergence of the Supreme Being; Sadler expects it to spread through the whole master universe
w09.012: Growth beyond the subabsolute levels; it characterizes the Cosmos Infinite
w09.013: The reasoning behind the first row runs as follows. The universes of time and space begin when the force organizers start to manipulate the space potency of the Unqualified Absolute. Yet nothing suggests that either the force organizers or the Unqualified Absolute had any part in the physical appearance of the central universe. It follows that our present manner of growth was not at work in the Havona age, a conclusion Sadler carries forward from his earlier appendices.
w09.014: The second way of growing has two forms: the pre-Supreme growth now taking place in the superuniverses, and the post-Supreme growth that will unfold in outer space after the Supreme Being has emerged. Sadler holds that both reach into Havona as well. Havona is part of the grand universe and of the master universe, and so with the opening of the second age it began to share in the cycle of growth. The third way is one that Sadler supposes will come into operation only after the master universe is finished and the Ultimate has emerged. The Urantia Book gives it no name, and it should be read entirely as his hypothesis.
w09.015: 2. The Sources of Growth: the Original, the Actual, and the Potential (orig. pp. 236–238)
w09.016: All experiential reality derives in the end from the seven Absolutes of infinity. Paper 115 regroups these seven under three headings, namely the Original, the Actual, and the Potential. The First Source and Center alone constitutes the Original; the Actual is the triodity of the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, and the Isle of Paradise; the Potential is the triodity of the Deity Absolute, the Unqualified Absolute, and the Universal Absolute.
w09.018: What draws Sadler's attention is the text's picture of the two triodities moving in opposite directions.
w09.020: The Actual is also the threefold center of gravity for spirit, mind, and energy. Spirit centers in the Eternal Son, mind in the Infinite Spirit, and physical energy in the Isle of Paradise. Whatever has already become actual is held in one or more of these three gravity circuits. The three Absolutes of the Potential, by contrast, are the inexhaustible wellsprings from which new spirit, new mind, and new matter arise. The Original belongs to neither group. He is the source of both, the one who sets their double motion going and holds it in balance.
w09.021: The double motion of the Original, the Actual, and the Potential. The new enters from the Potential at the periphery and is captured by the Actual at the center
w09.022: Growth, then, is not a matter of getting something out of nothing. As Sadler puts it, nothing yields only nothing. Growth is a kind of transaction in which reality passes from the level of the potential to the level of the actual.
w09.024: For spirit and for matter, Sadler finds this route drawn fairly clearly in the text. Spirit comes out of the potentiality of the Deity Absolute and is caught by the spirit gravity of the Eternal Son; cosmic force comes out of the space presence of the Unqualified Absolute and is caught by Paradise gravity. He candidly adds that the account of mind is less distinct. The mind circuit of the Conjoint Actor is dependable, yet not every mind reaction can be foreseen, and the text names the functioning of the Universal Absolute as one reason for this [9:6.8].
w09.025: 3. The Maturing of Potentials: Stepping the Absolute Down to the Finite (orig. pp. 238–239)
w09.026: A difficulty now appears. The three Absolutes of the Potential are, quite literally, absolute. But the growth of the master universe is a subabsolute process, taking place on finite and absonite levels.
w09.028: Someone, then, must reduce absolute potentiality to a scale that subabsolute beings can handle. Sadler concludes that this task falls to the Ultimate and the Supreme. Throughout the master universe it is the Ultimate who "creatively organizes" the Absolutes of potentiality [12:6.13], and the Supreme becomes the channel through which this organized potential flows down to the finite level [117:3.2]. Only potential matured in this way is placed in the hands of the creators of time and space. Seen from a wider angle, therefore, every act of creation is also an act of transformation.
w09.030: An electrical transformer makes the idea easy to grasp. High-voltage current from a power plant cannot be brought straight into a house; it must pass through a series of substations, each lowering the voltage, before a lamp can be lit. In Sadler's picture the Absolutes are the power plant, the Ultimate and the Supreme are the substations, and the Creator Sons together with their Creative Spirit consorts are the hands that use the current to make something real.
w09.033: One moment there is nothing; the next, 41,472 seraphim stand where nothing stood. Yet they did not come from nowhere, nor were they made of nothing. On Sadler's reading, the "what" was matured potential, and the "where" was the presence of the Supreme, in which that potential had been held in readiness. He adds the qualification that the Infinite Spirit and the Master Spirits also take part, in some manner, in this maturing, as when physical force ripens through energy into universe power.
w09.034: 4. The Character Experiential Deity Imparts to Growth (orig. p. 240)
w09.035: The Ultimate and the Supreme do more than scale potential down; they clothe it in their own character. Maturing potential rests within the master-universe omnipresence of the Ultimate and the grand-universe omnipresence of the Supreme before it becomes actual.
w09.037: Sadler compares this with the superuniverses. Each superuniverse is suffused with the nature of the Master Spirit who presides over it, and its natives carry that imprint all their lives.
w09.039: The same principle operates one level higher. The Supreme colors all growth in the grand universe, and the Ultimate colors all growth in the master universe. Here, Sadler suggests, lies the reason why finite creatures come at last to resemble the Supreme.
w09.040: 5. The Growth of the Supreme and the Growth of the Present Age (orig. pp. 241–242)
w09.041: To understand our own growth, we must understand the growth of the Supreme Being. Gathering statements from Papers 115 and 118, Sadler sets out three components of the Supreme. His spirit person derives from the Paradise Trinity; his almighty power derives from the divinity successes of God the Sevenfold; and the two are united by the supreme mind bestowed by the Conjoint Actor. The material out of which the Supreme grows, however, comes from the two triodities.
w09.043: The Supreme therefore lives within a double motion: He expands toward the Potential of outer space and He concentrates toward the Actual at the center. All finite reality is growing dynamically between these two poles [115:4.6].
w09.044: Sadler then takes a further step and reasons that every form of growth in the present age is possible because the Supreme is still incomplete. That we can make imperfect choices and so accumulate experience is due to our being participants in His growth.
w09.046: Growth of this kind belongs to the second age alone. It started with the onset of the Supreme's growth and will cease when that growth ceases; it did not exist in the Havona age and will not exist in the age of outer space. Evolutionary growth, Sadler remarks, is a very temporary condition in the long history of the master universe.
w09.049: Does every being in the grand universe share today in the growth of the Supreme? Sadler's answer is: for the most part, but not without exceptions. He sorts the inhabitants of the grand universe into four classes according to their relation to growth.
w09.050: Four growth conditions among grand-universe inhabitants (Sadler's classification)
w09.052: Trinity-origin beings and their Trinity-embraced associates (Divine Counselors, Mighty Messengers, and others)
w09.053: Mortals, midwayers, seraphim; local universe Sons and Spirits; Havona natives in the second age
w09.054: Not growing now; held in reserve
w09.055: Withdrawn from grand-universe activity, residing on Vicegerington
w09.056: For the first class, the testimony of a Mighty Messenger speaks directly.
w09.058: The third class consists of beings who live within the present age without belonging to it. The Urantia Book describes them as reserved for the age to come [117:2.3]. The fourth class is taken up again in Appendix VIII. Taken together, the four classes show four modes of growth overlapping in the present age: the non-growing Havona pattern, the second-age pattern of growing with the Supreme, the post-Supreme pattern of waiting for the next age, and the post-ultimate pattern of standing wholly apart from the affairs of the present universes.
w09.061: In the first age Havona did not grow at all. In the second age, however, as it entered into relationship with the grand universe, it took on some of the features of superuniverse evolutionary growth [24:7.9]. Sadler uses this change as a clue for anticipating what will happen when the present age closes and the age of outer space opens.
w09.062: His argument goes like this. The static condition of eternal Havona was broken when God, by free will, set a cycle of growth in motion. In response, the potentials of the Supreme appeared and the Deity presence of the Ultimate came into place. This is the mechanism of experiential growth now in operation, and it is what underlies the functioning of Total Deity on seven levels at present [0:1.3]. Sadler's proposal is that when the Supreme Being has emerged, these seven levels will change as well.
w09.063: The seven functional levels of Total Deity, now and after the Supreme (Sadler's proposal)
w09.069: As grounds for the change at the fifth level, Sadler points to the text's description of transcendental growth.
w09.071: To the Other Side of the Cosmic Ledger
w09.072: The change at the sixth level goes deeper. Sadler speaks here of a "cosmic ledger." One column of the ledger lists the Potential and the other the Actual. At present the Supreme works on the side of the Potential: He is still growing, and within His presence He conditions potential and steps it down. Once His emergence is complete, however, the Supreme moves over to the side of the Actual, joining the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit there. He no longer steps potential down but works directly with the potential that the Ultimate has creatively organized.
w09.073: How potential becomes actual. After the Supreme, the stepping-down stage of the Supreme drops out (the right column is Sadler's inference)
w09.074: As a result one stage disappears from the maturing process. The principle of growth stays the same, but its method changes: no longer experiential evolution on the finite level, but experiential eventuation on the absonite level [115:2.4]. Sadler calls this post-finite, post-creature, post-Supreme growth, and defines it as transcendental growth directed toward ultimate status.
w09.076: According to Sadler, one thing at least is clear about post-Supreme growth: it will not resemble growth as we now experience it.
w09.078: The citizens of outer space will have no finite experience [31:10.11]. They will grow with the completed Supreme Being as their premise, but they will not take part in His growth [117:2.7]. Sadler offers a memorable comparison here. Before Grandfanda arrived, a Havona native would have found it hard to imagine an evolving creature; in the same way, we shall probably not be able to picture the growth of the outer-spacers until we actually meet them.
w09.079: Even so, this future is no distant concern for mortal finaliters. The Urantia Book attributes seven dimensions to mortal personality.
w09.081: Sadler interprets present growth within the Supreme as the realization of the first three dimensions, and post-Supreme growth as the unfolding of the next three, which the present age has no means of expressing.
w09.083: Growth after the Ultimate lies outside the scope of this appendix, which deals with the mechanisms of experiential growth. Sadler names it the existential-experiential mechanism and defers it to Appendices XX and XXVII. He does sketch its character briefly. Since the Ultimate stands on the "⟦Q 0:2.17⟧final creative levels⟦/Q⟧" [0:2.17], growth beyond Him must be supercreative; it must pass beyond the absonite levels, where time and space are transcended, to the absolute levels, which know neither time nor space. Its place is the coabsolute level described in Paper 106, where experientials are projected upon a field beyond the master universe [106:0.7].
w09.084: Sadler expects the finaliters to be involved even in this remote future. Fusion with the Adjuster confers "⟦Q 112:7.1⟧a phase of qualified potential absoluteness⟦/Q⟧" [112:7.1], and mortal personality possesses a seventh dimension capable of approaching the absolute. The appendix closes with the following passage.
w09.087: Several of the paragraph references Sadler gives in this appendix are in error. The definitions of the Original, the Actual, and the Potential are found in Paper 115, section 3 (115:3.6–13), whereas the original in several places cites section 5 of that paper. The passage calling the Creator Sons "transformative creators" is 118:4.7 (the original has 118:7.7), and the Mighty Messenger's admission is 117:2.4. In the summary, "112:6.6" and "112:6.13" are slips for 12:6.6 and 12:6.13. This book corrects these against the text when quoting.
w09.088: Existential reality does not grow; experiential reality does, and experiential growth requires the partnership of creator and creature.
w09.089: Sadler distinguishes three ways of growing: existential (the Havona age), experiential (pre-Supreme and post-Supreme), and existential-experiential (post-ultimate). The last is his own hypothesis.
w09.090: Everything new rises from the three Absolutes of the Potential and is captured by the three gravity circuits of the Actual. Growth is not something drawn from nothing but a transfer of reality from potential to actual.
w09.091: Absolute potential becomes usable by the creators only after it has been stepped down through the Ultimate and the Supreme to subabsolute levels; in the process experiential Deity stamps its own character on that potential.
w09.092: Growth in the present age is made possible by the incompleteness of the Supreme and is temporary, ending when His growth is finished.
w09.093: The inhabitants of the grand universe fall into four growth conditions: status of the previous age, of the present age, of the post-Supreme ages, and of the post-ultimate age.
w09.094: Sadler reasons that when the Supreme emerges He will move to the Actual side of the "cosmic ledger," and growth will change from finite evolution to absonite eventuation.
w09.097: Where Appendix VII traced the route by which potential matures, Appendix VIII examines the several ways in which matured potential becomes actual being: creation, trinitization, eventuation, fragmentation, evolution, emerging personalization, and the Deity embrace. Sadler searches the text for the scope and limits of each technique and compares them, stressing that what is created begins from a status it was given, while what evolves earns everything for itself. He ends with a bold footnote that interprets the phenomenon of "fourth creatures" by means of Mendel's ratio of inheritance.
w09.098: 1. The Many Roads from Potential to Actual (orig. p. 249)
w09.099: Those of us who live on an evolutionary world are used to the contrast between instantaneous creation and slow evolution. Yet these are not the only roads by which beings and things pass from the potential into the actual. The Urantia Book says that one and the same God works in three distinct ways.
w09.101: Several further techniques must be added. Creators and certain creatures can trinitize new beings. In the local universe both creators and creatures evolve. The Creative Spirit is a unique being, the local-universe focalization of the Infinite Spirit in the course of becoming personal; and creatures who receive a Deity embrace may undergo a change of status. Sadler gathers all of these under the heading of transformative techniques. Whatever comes into being, it never arises from nothing; it is always potential that has been transformed.
w09.102: The seven transformative techniques as Sadler arranges them, with representative examples
w09.104: Creativity on Paradise and Creativity in Time and Space
w09.105: Sadler begins with a caution about creation. A procedure that is standard in time and space need not hold in Havona, still less on Paradise. The Urantia Book does not treat creatorship as one divine attribute among others.
w09.107: Sadler takes creatorship here in a broad sense, covering every way of bringing anything into existence. Noting that the text places side by side beings who are "⟦Q 13:1.12⟧trinitized, created, eventuated, or eternalized⟦/Q⟧" [13:1.12], he conjectures that "eternalized" may refer to a supercreative act of Paradise Deity.
w09.108: On creation in time and space the text is far more specific. When the Paradise Trinity activates static potentials, the Ultimacy of Deity transforms "undifferentiated potentiality" into segregated and defined plans, and these plans come under the supervision of the Master Architects [118:4.6]. At the last stage, finite beings are made out of the potential of the Supreme. Force organizers change space-force into energy, power directors change energy into matter, and Life Carriers initiate the changes of life in lifeless matter [42:1.5]. The Supreme Creators do the same kind of work with higher divine energies.
w09.110: Does the domain of creation have boundaries? Sadler believes it does. Its inner boundary lies where God, as a person, enters into subinfinite relations with other persons. Its outer boundary is the "final creative level" on which God the Ultimate functions [0:2.17]. Creativity in the strict sense is subinfinite in quantity and subabsolute in quality; it operates only within the realm of relative reality.
w09.112: Within those boundaries Sadler distinguishes at least four kinds of creativity.
w09.113: The first is **unlimited creativity**. The number of Creator Sons keeps increasing, and the Creative Spirits go on producing seraphim without end. The second is **creativity limited by plans**. Unlike the Creator Sons, the Unions of Days are fixed in number.
w09.115: The reason is not that the Trinity could make no more. One Union of Days for each local universe fits the plan exactly, and there is no need for others. Sadler regards most orders of fixed number as limited in just this way, by a choice of their creators.
w09.116: The third is **creativity limited by circumstance**. Here the limit lies not in the creator's will but in the situation itself. The Seven Master Spirits are the classic case.
w09.118: Even the Deities, Sadler observes, do not alter mathematics. The same class includes the inability of the Eternal Son to pass on to the Creator Sons the power to make yet another creator [6:5.4], the fixed number of the Solitary Messengers, and the single Bright and Morning Star in each local universe.
w09.120: Sadler surmises that in each local universe some basic potential is used up by that first creation.
w09.121: At this point Sadler collects the "pattern beings and first-borns": the first-born Michael, the original pattern angels, Nambia the first Life Carrier of Nebadon, Gavalia the first Evening Star, and others. Their special standing may come from a difference in created nature, or simply from the fact of having been first. Grandfanda provides his contrast. As the first mortal to reach Havona, Grandfanda was probably no different in nature from other ascenders; he heads the mortal finaliter corps merely because he arrived first. The first Michael, by contrast, was very likely unique from the moment of his creation, and Sadler leans toward that view.
w09.122: The fourth is **reflex and reflective creativity**, in which the act of one creator calls forth a creative act within another. Sadler is not sure the two belong together, but he gives an example of each. At the moment the Universal Father and the Eternal Son personalize a new Creator Son, a "supreme reaction of complement" takes place in the Infinite Spirit, and the potential of the future consort Spirit is segregated [17:6.3]. Sadler finds in this simultaneity the reason why our Michael is the personalization of concept number 611,121 and the Creative Spirit of Salvington bears the same number [33:1.1, 33:3.2]. His example of reflective creativity is the Universal Conciliators. When a Master Spirit creates a thousand Havona servitals, the Reflective Spirit that reflects that Master Spirit in each superuniverse at once brings forth a thousand conciliators, seven thousand in all [25:2.2].
w09.124: Sadler adds a footnote drawing a clear line between creation and procreation. The only procreating orders named in The Urantia Book are mortals, Material Sons, and midwayers. Creation is production, the bringing into existence of something new; procreation is reproduction, the repeating of one's own kind. A creator's intention fixes the nature of a new being within wide limits, whereas the intention of procreating parents settles only that a child will be born, not what its nature will be. In this sense Sadler considers the origin of the primary and secondary midwayers to be close to procreation. Each couple produced one thousand primary midwayers [77:1.5] or 248 secondary midwayers [77:6.4] before their capacity was exhausted, and all their offspring were of a single kind. What determined the nature of those offspring, Sadler suggests, was not the parents but the plans of higher creators.
w09.127: Trinitization resembles creation in that it brings forth new beings. Sadler nevertheless sees at least two differences. Creation is no secret, but trinitization belongs among the secrets of Vicegerington and Solitarington [13:1.12]. And whereas creation is confined to subabsolute levels, trinitization is not, for the Infinite Spirit, who appeared through the first trinitization, stands as an equal beside the Father and the Son.
w09.128: Sadler finds the word "trinitization" used in three senses in the text: the Trinity embrace, unlimited trinitization, and limited trinitization.
w09.130: The text also calls it trinitization when the Paradise Trinity embraces particular creatures. The Trinitized Sons of Attainment, of Selection, and of Perfection arise in this way and are assigned to the superuniverse governments. The embrace raises status but fixes growth.
w09.132: As a dissolved substance settles out of a solution, what would someday have been attained hardens all at once in the present. In Sadler's terms, the embraced finaliter receives in advance what he would eventually have gained as a spirit of the seventh stage [40:10.12].
w09.134: The difference between the remaining two senses shows up clearly in a table.
w09.135: Creation and the two kinds of trinitization (Sadler's comparison)
w09.137: Father and Son; two qualified creatures
w09.138: The parents become in some way one
w09.139: Equal in status to the parents
w09.142: Sadler believes that the unrevealed Deity-trinitized Sons arose through unlimited trinitization. He also notes that the text sometimes uses the word loosely, almost as a synonym for creation, as when it says that the Ancients of Days were all trinitized at the same moment [18:3.4].
w09.143: The prototype of limited trinitization is the origin of the Infinite Spirit. After that event the Father and the Son became one as the Father-Son; the Infinite Spirit is a Deity equal to Them; and there can be no second Infinite Spirit. Sadler thinks of this first event in three steps, dualization, trinitization, and Trinity formation, yet he holds that the order is only conceptual: in fact all three occurred together, and at no moment was Deity ever divided. Carried down the scale, the same principle reads as follows. When two infinite Deities trinitize, a third infinite Deity appears. When two subinfinite creators trinitize, a third subinfinite creator would result. The text merely reports the view that in future ages a closer union may come about between a Creator Son and a Divine Minister [56:7.7]; Sadler reads this as a trinitization by two creators. And when two creatures trinitize, a third creature results.
w09.144: The Time Range of Creature Trinitization
w09.145: Here Sadler notices an intriguing reversal. A Creator Son handles potential far more deeply and broadly than any pair of creatures. Yet along the axis of the ages he is more narrowly bound, for on becoming a Master Son he gives up the power to create wholly new types of creatures in the present universe age [21:5.6]. Creature trinitization, on the other hand, is not tied to the needs of the present age. It brings into actuality, ahead of time, potentials of the Supreme not yet realized, and its purpose appears to be preparation for future ages.
w09.146: Sadler divides the creature-trinitized sons into two groups. The Ascender-Trinitized Sons embody spirit potentials of the Almighty Supreme, the Paradise-Havona-Trinitized Sons those of the Supreme, and both groups are therefore "post-Supreme" sons. They serve in the inner Havona circuits, on the Paradise worlds of the Infinite Spirit, and in the local universes, and they will later work as the Corps of Trinitized Finaliters in outer space or gather at the superuniverse headquarters at the close of this age. The Trinitized Sons of Destiny, trinitized jointly by a finaliter and a Paradise-Havoner, embody the Supreme-Ultimate Mind and are therefore "post-ultimate" sons [22:7.14]. They cannot serve in the present universes; they withdraw to Vicegerington under the custody of the Architects of the Master Universe. Sadler's conclusion is that the creations of creators are fitted to the needs of the present age, whereas the trinitizations of creatures look toward the ages to come.
w09.149: Eventuation is the word used for the way the Transcendentalers come into being. The text says that its authors know their origin but have been instructed not to disclose it [31:9.2], yet it does explain why this particular word was chosen.
w09.151: Sadler reasons that a word chosen precisely to avoid meaninglessness must carry meaning, and he consults the dictionary sense of "eventuate": to come about in the end, to result. Its root, "event," denotes in relativity theory an occurrence at a single point of space-time. The usage in the text closest to this sense is the following.
w09.153: No one plans or builds a system. When three or more things stand within one frame, a system simply arises. The text's description of the Trinity as a superadditive reality that "eventuates" from the union of the three Paradise Deities [104:2.4] uses the word in the same way. To eventuate is to happen inevitably, because the outcome was latent in the situation all along.
w09.154: Compossibility and the Plans of God
w09.155: Sadler connects this intuition with the principle of consistency. The text says that omnipotence carries with it a corollary called "compossibility."
w09.157: Once God makes a circle, circularity becomes the nature of every circle, and a square circle is impossible. Again, God does not "create" brotherhood as a separate act: the moment He becomes the Father of all persons, brotherhood follows from that fatherhood of itself [12:7.10]. On the strength of these two examples Sadler proposes an analogy. When God forms a plan, everything eternally required for the inception, realization, and consummation of that plan appears with it, inevitably; otherwise it would be no plan but a daydream. In a witty turn of phrase, Sadler says that God knows the subjunctive mood well enough, but thinks and plans in the "eternal indicative."
w09.158: Seen in this light, the Architects of the Master Universe are beings who appeared in accordance with God's concept of the master universe at the moment He conceived it. They are not creatures, since they were never created, and they are not creators, since they do not create. Sadler calls them "inceptors": beings who open the work long before the creators step onto the stage of space. Taking as his clue the text's remark that the Deity Absolute may have had a part in how the Transcendentalers originated [31:8.3], he further conjectures that the plan of God, passing through the Trinity, echoed in the Deity Absolute, and that the Deity Absolute then precipitated out of potential the beings the plan required. Sadler himself labels all of this speculative reasoning.
w09.160: The Adjusters and the other fragments of the Father come into being by fragmentation. Sadler groups with it three cases in which divine spirit is individualized. First, the Infinite Spirit and the Creative Spirits fragment a premind spirit, and ascenders fused with such a spirit become Spirit-fused mortals. Second, the Eternal Son cannot fragment Himself, but a Creator Son can individualize a portion of his spirit, and those fused with it become Son-fused mortals [30:1.102]. Third, the Universal Father, on the prepersonal level, detaches fragments of His Deity nature, and those who fuse with such an Adjuster become Father-fused mortals.
w09.161: Fragmentation, too, has its secret: it is the secret of Divinington. An Adjuster is subinfinite in quantity but undiluted Deity in quality [107:1.2]. Personalized Adjusters reach a unique status.
w09.165: Sadler defines evolution as creativity in time. Because time divides a process into small steps, the creatures within it can perceive change, understand it in some measure, and take part in it directly. Evolution also has its secret, the secret of Ascendington: the mystery of the immortal soul growing within the mortal mind [13:1.22].
w09.166: The difference between creation and evolution lies in the starting point. A created being begins from a status it did not earn; an evolving being earns everything it has. Sadler offers three examples. The Ancients of Days, perfect by creation alone, illustrate **pure creation**. The seraphim, who start from a created status and grow until they become co-ordinate with the seconaphim, illustrate **creation plus evolution**. Mortals illustrate **pure evolution**: born of parents, they acquire one by one the status of faith son, ascending son, spirit being, Havona pilgrim, Paradise arrival, and finaliter. Even the coming of the Adjuster waits upon the first moral decision.
w09.167: Evolution yields values that creation cannot produce. Of the Technical Advisers the text says:
w09.169: Decision and Action: The Practical Mechanism of Growth
w09.170: How, then, does a person actually grow? Sadler begins from a brief prescription in the text.
w09.172: The text elsewhere calls action "⟦Q 110:6.17⟧completion of decisions⟦/Q⟧" [110:6.17]. Sadler unfolds this into three steps: growth begins with honesty, is realized through courage, and is completed by actually doing something. If life is a process that takes place between an organism and its environment [112:1.13], then decision followed by action quickens the exchange between the self and its environment. For a finite creature, that environment is ultimately the immanence of the Supreme. Hence, on Sadler's interpretation, finite growth consists in "taking in" the potential of the Supreme through decision and "digesting" it into actuality through action. The Adjuster is the one who builds the soul, yet personality itself has a creative quality, "⟦Q 112:2.15⟧the evolution of dominance⟦/Q⟧" [112:2.15]. Nor is the environment passive.
w09.176: Personality does not arise of its own accord.
w09.178: The text speaks of two types of personality, First Source and Third Source [9:8.10]. Sadler, however, identifies two cases that fit neither. One is the Creative Spirit, said to be "⟦Q 9:8.11⟧in a class by themselves⟦/Q⟧" [9:8.11]; the other is experiential Deity, which is still passing through "⟦Q 10:5.5⟧the prepersonal eras of experiential-power development⟦/Q⟧" [10:5.5]. Because personality is gradually dawning in both, Sadler calls this "emerging personalization."
w09.179: The Seven Stages of a Creative Spirit
w09.180: Sadler regroups into four sets the seven stages of a Creative Spirit described in Paper 17. In the first three stages the Spirit is prepersonal. She starts out as a potential segregated within the Infinite Spirit, undergoes preliminary training on the Havona circuits, and, in answer to the "prayer of identification" of a Master Spirit, appears for the first time as a distinct entity and goes forth with a Creator Son to a local universe. In the fourth stage, when the intention to create life is declared, the personalization ceremonies are held on Paradise, and with "the primary eruption" she is personalized for the first time [17:6.7]. In the fifth and sixth stages, following the Creator Son's "⟦Q 33:3.6⟧Proclamation of Equality⟦/Q⟧" [33:3.6], her personal qualities increase further. The seventh stage is "⟦Q 17:6.10⟧the unrevealed career⟦/Q⟧" [17:6.10].
w09.181: The seven stages of a Creative Spirit in Sadler's four groupings. Sadler surmises that completed personalization will come with the emergence of the Supreme Being
w09.182: Sadler points out with care that nowhere does the text call a Creative Spirit a person without some qualification. It says only that the Creator Son regards her as a person, that she is a person "to all practical intents and purposes," and that she attains personality status. Sadler does not think these qualifications accidental. He infers that from the fourth stage onward the Creative Spirit is a person in the making, and that her personalization will be completed only in the seventh stage. The moment, he suggests, will be when every one of the seven hundred thousand local universes has become settled in light and life, which is to say when the Supreme Being emerges.
w09.183: A Repetition of the Infinite Spirit
w09.184: Sadler now advances a bold theory: in time and space the Creative Spirit is re-enacting what the Infinite Spirit once did on Paradise in eternity.
w09.186: Sadler notes that the text calls the Infinite Spirit, at the time Havona appeared, the "executive agency" of the Father-Son partnership [8:1.3], and he reads this as a hint of a personality not yet completed. Had Havona been created in stages, one might have observed the Infinite Spirit in what would look like the process of becoming a person. But the central creation appeared as an eternal existence all at once, and so did the Infinite Spirit.
w09.187: Deities Who Depend upon Their Creations
w09.188: From this comparison Sadler draws a generalization that sorts creators and Deities into two classes.
w09.189: Personalization and its relation to a creation (Sadler's classification)
w09.191: The Eternal Son, Creator Sons, the Seven Master Spirits
w09.192: Personalized in dependence on a creation
w09.193: When all local universes are perfected
w09.194: When the seven superuniverses are completed
w09.195: When the master universe is completed
w09.196: When the inner realms of the Cosmos Infinite appear (Sadler's conjecture)
w09.197: According to the text, the spirit nature and personality of God the Supreme have their source in the Paradise Trinity [0:8.10]. It also relates that when the Supreme Being first acted creatively, after the creation of the Reflective Spirits, a reaction occurred in the Deity Absolute that gave Him "⟦Q 17:2.2⟧new personality prerogatives⟦/Q⟧" [17:2.2]. Sadler finds this closely parallel to the stage-by-stage personalization of a Creative Spirit.
w09.199: The Deity embrace resembles the Trinity embrace, but whereas it changes status, it does not halt further growth. The text gives only three examples. Cherubim and sanobim left behind when their seraphic seniors depart are embraced by the Creative Spirit and become Mansion World Teachers; after long service they may be embraced again and become seraphim [38:8.5–6]. The third example takes place on Paradise.
w09.201: The Havona servitals who disappear in this way appear to become graduate guides. Sadler confesses that he does not know what the expressions "Paradise Central Shining" and "Luminous Persons" refer to. Since the text is highly precise whenever it chooses to be, he judges the vagueness to be deliberate. When fuller explanation would require disclosing more than is intended, the text chooses ambiguity, remaining true to the facts while leaving room for the reader's interpretation.
w09.202: 9. Footnote: Fourth Creatures and Mendel's Ratio (orig. pp. 288–292)
w09.204: In the closing footnote of the appendix Sadler turns to genetics. Put four white checkers and four black checkers in a hat, draw them out two at a time to form pairs, and repeat many times: the results approach one white-white pair, two white-black pairs, and one black-black pair. This is the familiar formula (a+b)² = a² + 2ab + b². It is the same 3-to-1 ratio that Mendel obtained by crossing tall peas with short ones. Because the dominant trait masks the recessive, three out of four look alike outwardly, though in fact they comprise one pure strain and two hybrids.
w09.205: The Urantia Book never mentions Mendel, but it does use the expression "fourth creatures." Sadler observes that "one in four" is just another way of saying "three to one."
w09.207: Mendel's ratio as Sadler applies it to "fourth creatures." When two hereditary factors meet, two pure types and two hybrids appear in the ratio 1:2:1
w09.209: Sadler finds four instances in the text. First, the Havona servitals are brought forth by the Master Spirits acting together with the Supreme Power Directors, so they inherit both a spiritual factor (S) and a physical factor (p). Noting that the servitals who become graduate guides number "nearly one in four," Sadler surmises that these are the pure (SS) member among each three outwardly similar spiritual servitals. Second, the Universal Conciliators serve in groups of four. On Sadler's reading, the Judge-Arbiter is pure spiritual (SS), the semimaterial Divine Executioner is the fourth creature (pp), and the other two are hybrids [25:2.5].
w09.210: The third case is an instance of physical dominance.
w09.212: Of the sixty-seven children of Adamson and Ratta, sixteen were such "fourth children," and they became the parents of the secondary midwayers. Sixteen out of sixty-seven is 23.88 percent, close to the theoretical 25 percent. Sadler goes further and asks whether the loss of this spiritual latent factor from the human race might explain why the Greeks, descendants of the Adamsonites, excelled in art and philosophy yet lagged in religion. The idea has no basis in the text, and Sadler himself leaves it as a question.
w09.213: Fourth, the cherubim and sanobim also have fourth creatures.
w09.215: Since these beings come from a single Creative Spirit, there would seem to be only one hereditary factor. Sadler finds his answer in the fact that the Creative Spirit functions as a creator not only in the spiritual domain but in the morontial domain as well. He then matches the text's division of cherubim into three classes, ascension candidates, mid-phase cherubim, and morontia cherubim [38:8.1], with the 1:2:1 pattern of SS, Sm, and mm. Sadler closes by suggesting that this principle may be widely at work among many orders the text does not mention.
w09.217: Applying Mendel's ratio is Sadler's own interpretation, resting on the text's "fourth creatures" and its figure of three to one. What the text itself states is limited to this: Havona servitals, the conciliating commissions, and cherubim and sanobim have fourth creatures [38:7.6], and every fourth child of Adamson was unusual. That the pure-strain servitals become graduate guides, and the question about Greek civilization, are conjectures about matters left unrevealed. Also, the reference 38:4.6 that the original gives for the second embrace of cherubim appears to mean 38:8.6.
w09.218: Beings and things pass from potential to actual by more roads than creation and evolution. Sadler distinguishes seven techniques: creation, trinitization, eventuation, fragmentation, evolution, emerging personalization, and the Deity embrace.
w09.219: The domain of creation lies between God's relations as a person (the inner boundary) and the final creative level of God the Ultimate (the outer boundary). Within it are four types: unlimited creativity, creativity limited by plans, creativity limited by circumstance, and reflex creativity.
w09.220: Trinitization belongs among the secrets and is not confined to subabsolute levels. Limited trinitization unites the parents, produces offspring equal to them, and can happen only once.
w09.221: Creature trinitization has a wider time range than the creations of creators, since it looks beyond the needs of the present age to the post-Supreme and post-ultimate ages.
w09.222: Eventuation is the inevitable appearance of what was latent in the plans of God; Sadler infers that the Transcendentalers, being neither creators nor creatures, are best called "inceptors."
w09.223: Evolution is creativity in time. An evolving being earns everything for itself and grows by turning the potential of the Supreme into actuality through decision and action.
w09.224: Sadler generalizes that the Creative Spirits, the Infinite Spirit, and the experiential Deities complete their personalization when their creations are complete.
w09.225: Sadler interprets the "fourth creatures" through Mendel's 3-to-1 ratio, an interpretation the text itself does not state.
